narr: Heavy rain fell across the area.
ev: Widespread flash flooding in and around town with 4 to 6 inches of depth in most areas.
Overflowing ditches and flooded fields resulted in water flowing over McNair Road near Meadville.
A section of Seale road was washed out near a culvert in Roxie.
Hwy 43 flooded in 3 locations with water across the roadway.
Portions of Pattison Tillman Road were flooded and closed.
Heavy rain led to flash flooding along the MS Highway 28 corridor. Dentville Road near South Raymond Road was flooded, and parts of MS Highway 28 were flooded.
Widespread flooding occurred in the Georgetown area.
Water was across the road with culverts flooding over driveways near the corner of Old Jackson Road and Ford Road.

With rainfall totals of over 7 inches in a 2 to 3 hour period, flash flooding affected roads and a few structures in areas of Franklin County in and around the Roxie areas. A culvert and section of Seale Road washed out.
Flooding occurred across the roadway on S Pearson Road near Grand at Pearl Apartments.
Fox Hall Road was closed due to flash flooding along parts of the road.
Sylvarena Road at Lott Smith Rd was flooded.
Water was over MS Highway 481 for a short period of time.
MS Highway 540 was flooded with water across the roadway, and MS Highway 43 was flooded over in three locations.
A few roads were flooded in Sontag.
Flood prone roads were covered with 4 to 8 inches of water, and other roads were closed with cars stalled in floodwaters.
Multiple rural roads were flooded in northwest Lincoln County as numerous creeks overspread their banks.
An area near the intersection of US Highway 84 and Main Street was flooded, and floodwaters entered a nearby home. Water flowed over McNair Road near Meadville.
